page: Microsoft Azure B4ps_v2 is a burstable virtual machine belonging to the Bpsv2 server family. It features an ARM64 architecture powered by an Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor running at 3.0 GHz. This configuration provides 4 physical cores and 4 vCPUs with a 1:1 thread-to-core ratio, meaning hyperthreading is absent. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with hardware-accelerated AES cryptography support. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable, and it does not include any GPU resources.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the B4ps_v2 delivers moderate CPU performance. In stress-ng testing, it achieves a single-core score of 1822.69 and a multi-core score of 7252.95, both falling within the average range. Memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks is also average, measuring 46.07 GB/sec for read operations and 29.04 GB/sec for write operations. However, small-block cached read bandwidth is relatively weak at 282.3 GB/sec. The instance shows weaker performance in complex computational tasks, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1109.0 and a multi-core score of 3672.0. Cryptographic performance is poor, as evidenced by a Passmark encryption score of 647.61, which is attributed to the lack of advanced vector and matrix extensions.

Given its burstable CPU allocation and ARM64 architecture, the B4ps_v2 offers a cost-efficient profile for workloads with variable CPU utilization. The burstable model allows resources to scale up during peak demands while maintaining a lower baseline cost during idle periods. This resource density makes it suitable for lightweight database operations, static web serving, and general-purpose development or testing environments. It is less suited for continuous high-performance computing, intensive cryptography, or large language model inference due to its lower benchmark scores in those areas.
